claims.text: An actively learned ML interatomic potential trained on ab initio configurations from both high-temperature solid and liquid states will better represent the diverse atomic configurations of HEA liquids than static EAM references.
Replacing EAM references with the proposed ML potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method is applicable to multicomponent HEAs in both solid and liquid phases near their melting temperatures, including refractory systems such as HfNbTaTiZr.

The proposed reference is an ML potential, such as a neural-network or Gaussian approximation potential, actively and iteratively trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots from solid and liquid states.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9Tm to Tm for HEAs whose melting temperature exceeds 1500 °C.
The ML potential represents local environments spanning a wide distribution of coordination numbers and bonding arrangements.
Representing diverse local environments enables the ML potential to capture many-body interactions characteristic of high-temperature disorder.
Iterative learning from a broad ab initio configuration set captures liquid configurations that static EAM potentials miss.
Capturing a broader range of configurations increases phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will decrease by approximately 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed ML reference will produce a smoother thermodynamic-integration pathway.
The proposed ML reference will require fewer thermodynamic-integration sampling points.
The proposed ML reference will improve agreement of calculated free energies with direct ab initio benchmarks.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately capture the range of atomic configurations in high-temperature HEA liquids and consequently produce larger integration-path mismatches.
The intervention's advantage will be less pronounced in simpler alloys or at lower temperatures, where atomic configurations are less diverse.
Direct benchmarks of ML potentials for complex HEA liquid states are limited.
